=== Mid Calder working father, 23 October 2026 ===

'''New working father, 23 October 2026: unknown → Andrew Glasgow-1239, 42% possible.''' Select Andrew Glasgow-1239 as the possible working father of Alexander Glasgow-3612. The inspected 17 April 1757 Mid Calder transcript names Alexander, father Andrew Glasgow and mother Janet Young. The adult Alexander’s uncertain 1760 birth and Newton/Midlothian family are compatible with this child: a 1757 child would be about 20 at his son George’s reported 1777 birth. The three-year difference from an uncertain birth field is not an exclusion. Andrew-1239’s 21 December 1729 Livingston baptism places a documented Andrew in the neighbouring parish and the right generation, aged about 27 in 1757. This is the preferred available regional and chronological reconstruction, rather than leaving the named-parent lead entirely outside the working tree.

42% is a subjective assessment of the complete adult Alexander → Andrew-1239 profile pair, including both the 1757 child-to-adult identification and the identification of the named Andrew with the Livingston child. Neither identity is proved by a shared occupation, witness, holding or later parent clause. The record-defined father’s given name and surname are explicit; that does not make this later profile pair confident. Andrew-3052, associated with Janet Clerk and an earlier Alexander household, remains an unselected possible alternative at 32%; a different spouse is not an exclusion. Other or unrepresented Andrews remain possible. No percentages are multiplied, and the two Andrew hypotheses are not independent propositions. Janet Young is the recorded mother but no modern mother identity is assigned. All vital fields, spouses and existing child links remain unchanged.

=== Possible Andrew Glasgow, Leith society and merchant notices, 1779–1790 ===
Andrew Glasgow is a named signatory in a Leith and St Anthony’s journeymen-society notice dated 3 February 1779, under the grouped Preses to annotation.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601805253/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1779-02-09, p.7].</ref>

Andrew Glasgow, merchant in Kirkgate, Leith, is named as a contact where impost warrants may be obtained.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601818940/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1790-12-07, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601819059/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1790-12-10, p.2].</ref>

The grouped annotation "Preses to" does not independently identify Andrew’s society or trade. The Leith name and place make the 1779 and 1790 occurrences compatible, without proving that they concern the same man. Being a contact for warrants does not establish that he held a tax office.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3052]]. Uncertain 1720 Midlothian birth is compatible; no Leith society or signature connection.

=== Possible Robert Glasgow and father Andrew, miller at Calder, 1772 ===
Robert Glasgow is listed as son of Andrew Glasgow, miller at Calder, in an Edinburgh magistrates’ notice dated 28 November 1772.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395731868/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1772-11-28, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395732022/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1772-11-30, p.3].</ref>

The notice directly identifies its Robert as the son of Andrew, miller at Calder. It does not distinguish East from West Calder or identify the mother. The two newspaper issues repeat the same family statement, not independent evidence of the later profile identities.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3052]]. For the named father Andrew, The recorded dates give uncertain birth in 1720 at Kirknewton/East Calder, allowing adult fatherhood in 1772. The account has no recorded miller occupation or proved relationship to the newspaper Robert; its sibling relationship to Glasgow-1445 is tree-derived only.
